proof:
Source: steps 1, 2, 3(a), 4, 5(a) and 6(i)–(ii) of the parent-supplied proof of fiw_tl_ald_local_differentiation. They are specialized to one weight (M, θ) and a general integrand f (the parent's g), with H replaced by an arbitrary measure μ; that proof uses no property of H. The closed-ball Lebesgue differentiation step is derived directly from Mathlib in step 5. It is the same argument as the sibling node closed_ball_lebesgue_point, repeated here so that this proof is self-contained.

Notation: K := B̄_r(y) = closedBall y r, S := M ∩ K, B_s := B̄_s(x) = closedBall x s, t⁺ := ENNReal.ofReal t, ν := (μ⌞S).withDensity (z ↦ θ(z)⁺) and λ := μ⌞(M ∩ B_r(y)).

1. Null-measurability. K is closed, hence measurable, so S is μ-null-measurable. Therefore μ⌞S-a.e. z lies in S (ae_restrict_mem₀). Likewise M ∩ B_r(y) is μ-null-measurable, since open balls are measurable.

2. Finiteness. ν(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻_S θ⁺ dμ ≤ ∫⁻_S ‖θ‖ₑ dμ < ∞, because θ is μ-integrable on S. Formally, isFiniteMeasure_withDensity_ofReal applied to the HasFiniteIntegral part of IntegrableOn θ S μ gives IsFiniteMeasure ν. Hence ν is s-finite and locally finite.

3. Reverse absolute continuity. θ is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞S (part of its integrability), so θ⁺ is AEMeasurable for μ⌞S (AEMeasurable.ennreal_ofReal). For μ⌞S-a.e. z we have z ∈ M, so θ(z) > 0 and θ(z)⁺ ≠ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pos). By withDensity_absolutelyContinuous', μ⌞S ≪ ν.

4. f ∈ L¹(ν).
(a) ENNReal.ofReal t is by definition the coercion of t.toNNReal, so ν = (μ⌞S).withDensity (z ↦ ↑(θ(z).toNNReal)). The function z ↦ θ(z).toNNReal is AEMeasurable for μ⌞S (AEMeasurable.real_toNNReal).
(b) By integrable_withDensity_iff_integrable_smul₀, f is ν-integrable iff z ↦ θ(z).toNNReal • f(z) is μ⌞S-integrable.
(c) For μ⌞S-a.e. z we have θ(z) > 0, hence θ(z).toNNReal • f(z) = θ(z)·f(z) (NNReal.smul_def, Real.coe_toNNReal, smul_eq_mul).
(d) z ↦ θ(z)·f(z) is μ⌞S-integrable by hypothesis. By (c) and Integrable.congr, z ↦ θ(z).toNNReal • f(z) is μ⌞S-integrable, so f is ν-integrable by (b).
(e) In particular f is AEStronglyMeasurable for ν, hence for μ⌞S by step 3 (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac).

5. Lebesgue differentiation for ν along closed balls.
(a) ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional real normed space. So it is a second-countable metric space with its Borel σ-algebra, and it has the Besicovitch covering property (instHasBesicovitchCovering).
(b) Since ν is s-finite, Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν is a Vitali family for ν.
(c) Because f ∈ L¹(ν), f is locally integrable for ν (Integrable.locallyIntegrable), and ν is locally finite. VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div then gives, for ν-a.e. x: (∫⁻_a ‖f(z) − f(x)‖ₑ dν(z)) / ν(a) → 0 as a → x along (Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν).filterAt x.
(d) By Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt ν x, s ↦ B_s tends to that filter as s → 0⁺. Composing (Tendsto.comp) gives, for ν-a.e. x: Q(s) := (∫⁻_{B_s} ‖f(z) − f(x)‖ₑ dν(z)) / ν(B_s) → 0 as s → 0⁺.

6. Transfer to λ. M ∩ B_r(y) ⊆ S because ball y r ⊆ closedBall y r. So λ ≤ μ⌞S (Measure.restrict_mono), and hence λ ≪ μ⌞S ≪ ν (Measure.absolutelyContinuous_of_le, step 3, AbsolutelyContinuous.trans). By AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le, the conclusion of step 5 holds for λ-a.e. x. Also, by step 1 and ae_restrict_mem₀, x ∈ M ∩ B_r(y) for λ-a.e. x. Fix x with both properties (filter_upwards). It remains to prove the stated limit at x.

7. Identification on small balls. Since x ∈ B_r(y), ρ := r − dist(x, y) > 0, and (0, ρ) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). For s ∈ (0, ρ) we have s + dist(x, y) ≤ r. So B_s ⊆ K (closedBall_subset_closedBall'), and therefore B_s ∩ S = M ∩ B_s. The ball B_s is measurable.
(i) ∫⁻_{B_s} ‖f(z) − f(x)‖ₑ dν(z) = ∫⁻_{B_s} θ(z)⁺·‖f(z) − f(x)‖ₑ d(μ⌞S)(z) = ∫⁻_{M∩B_s} θ(z)⁺·‖f(z) − f(x)‖ₑ dμ(z).
- The first equality is setLIntegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul₀. Its hypotheses hold: θ⁺ is AEMeasurable for μ⌞S by step 3, and z ↦ ‖f(z) − f(x)‖ₑ is AEMeasurable for μ⌞S by step 4(e) (AEStronglyMeasurable.sub with a constant, then .enorm).
- The second equality is Measure.restrict_restrict together with B_s ∩ S = M ∩ B_s.
(ii) ν(B_s) = ∫⁻_{B_s} θ⁺ d(μ⌞S) = ∫⁻_{M∩B_s} θ⁺ dμ, by withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict and B_s ∩ S = M ∩ B_s.
Hence for every s ∈ (0, ρ), Q(s) equals the quotient in the statement. The two functions of s therefore agree eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, and Tendsto.congr' transfers the limit 0 of step 5 to the stated quotient. This holds for λ-almost every x, which is the claim. ∎
key_steps: ν := (μ⌞(M∩K)).withDensity θ⁺ with K = B̄_r(y) is finite, because θ ∈ L¹(μ⌞(M∩K)) (isFiniteMeasure_withDensity_ofReal). Also μ⌞(M∩K) ≪ ν, because θ > 0 on M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous').
f ∈ L¹(ν): integrable_withDensity_iff_integrable_smul₀ reduces this to θ·f ∈ L¹(μ⌞(M∩K)), since θ.toNNReal•f = θf a.e. Hence f is also AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞(M∩K) (mono_ac).
Lebesgue differentiation for ν along closed balls: VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div for Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν, composed with Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt ν x.
Transfer: λ = μ⌞(M ∩ B_r(y)) ≤ μ⌞(M∩K) ≪ ν, so the limit holds λ-a.e. (AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le). Also x ∈ M ∩ B_r(y) λ-a.e.

For 0 < s < r − dist(x, y), B̄_s(x) ⊆ K, so the ν-quotient equals the μ-quotient (setLIntegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul₀, withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict). Conclude by Tendsto.congr'.
